newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee dips on higher dollar demand.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee dips on higher dollar demand.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee, which opened lower on overseas strengh of the dollar, continued to ease on Wednesday due to commercial demand for the greenback, dealers said.
At 0510 GMT the rupee was at 59.10 to the dollar after opening at 59. The rupee closed at 58.90 to the dollar on Monday, the previous trading day.
"Trading is moderate with some commercial demand and speculation after the Central Bank revalued the dollar aggressively on its international strength," said a Deutsche Bank dealer.
The Central Bank pushed up the dollar by eight local cents, fixing buying and selling prices at 57.9794 and 59.1507.

Low call money rates were also conducive to speculation, dealers said. Overnight call money was at 8.125 percent after opening at 8.75 percent. Forward rates were also seen easing on the back of low money rates.
"One-month forwards which are now at a premium of 22 to 28 cents, should fall to about 20 cents soon," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer.
